title: Laxative treatment perturbs gut microbiome composition and metabolism in humans independent of short-term fiber consumption: a randomized controlled crossover intervention study.
abstract: Gastrointestinal transit time is a major ecological determinant of the human gut microbiome, yet causal evidence that disentangles the effects of diet from those of the gut environment remains limited. Here, we conducted a randomized, controlled crossover trial in healthy adults (nine females, four males) consuming fully standardized high-fiber (40 g/d) or low-fiber (10 g/d) diets to assess how manipulating the gut environment using an osmotic laxative (Movicol) affects gut microbial composition

title: Microbiota-Bile acid decoupling contributes to altered postnatal growth and metabolism in sFGR: a twin-paired dynamic study with FMT validation.
abstract: Selective fetal growth restriction (sFGR) increases the risk of adverse long-term metabolic outcomes, yet the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Bile acids (BAs) mediate gut microbiota-host metabolic crosstalk, and their early-life perturbation may underlie sFGR-associated health risks. title: Helicobacter pylori in the pediatric gastric niche: from pathobiont to pathogen and the pre-adolescent window of opportunity.
abstract: Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) is a definitive adult carcinogen, yet pediatric management remains conservative due to the rarity of acute complications. This review addresses a paradigm shift, evaluating whether H. pylori behaves as a tolerated pathobiont or an active pathogen within the pediatric gastric niche. title: Akkermansia muciniphila-driven metabolic homeostasis in cross-organ communications and diseases.
abstract: Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila) has emerged as a next-generation probiotic with broad effects on host metabolic homeostasis and immune modulation via cross-organ communications. However, the effects of A. muciniphila are not uniformly beneficial and vary with strain, diet, microbial community, host state, and disease context. title: Combined high-intensity interval training and propionate supplementation attenuate ventricular remodeling and cognitive decline in a rat model of heart failure.
abstract: Heart failure (HF) is a complex clinical syndrome characterized by progressive ventricular remodeling, chronic inflammation, and functional decline, often accompanied by cognitive deficits. Although pharmacological therapies improve symptoms, residual morbidity persists, highlighting the need for effective non‑pharmacological strategies. title: The microbiota-gut-brain axis in ischemic stroke recovery: Mechanistic insights, evidence gaps, and translational opportunities.
abstract: The microbiota-gut-brain axis has been implicated in outcome after ischemic stroke, but acute neuroprotection, later functional status, and recovery trajectories are distinct endpoints. This narrative review examines immune and metabolic mechanisms against that distinction. title: B12 promotes an inflammatory microenvironment, gut dysbiosis, and potentiates myeloid-biased clonal hematopoiesis.
abstract: Vitamin B12 is a bacterially derived tetrapyrrole and essential cofactor in human metabolism. Elevated serum B12 has been associated with clonal hematopoiesis (CH) and increased risk of myeloid malignancy, though its role in myeloid disease remains unclear. Given its structural similarity to heme, a damage-associated molecular pattern, we hypothesized that B12 may also exert immunomodulatory effects that influence CH. title: Ultrahigh-Temperature Processing Reduces miR-26a in Bovine Milk Exosomes and Weakens Their Anti-Inflammatory Activity by Impairing TAK1-MAPK Suppression and Gut Microbiota Modulation.
abstract: Ultrahigh-temperature (UHT) sterilization ensures dairy safety, but its effects on the biological activity of bovine milk exosomes (BMEs) remain unclear. Using a dextran sulfate sodium (DSS)-induced colitis mouse model, we compared raw milk exosomes (Raw_MEs), UHT-treated exosomes (UHT_MEs), and bta-miR-26a-loaded liposomes (MiR_Lipo). journal: Journal of agricultural and food chemistry

title: Sodium butyrate combined with ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains attenuates alcoholic liver disease by restoring gut-liver homeostasis.
abstract: Alcoholic liver disease (ALD) is characterized by hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammation, and intestinal barrier dysfunction, while limited effective pharmacological interventions remain currently available. This study investigated the protective effects of sodium butyrate (NaB), alone and in combination with newly isolated ethanol-metabolizing Lactobacillus strains on ALD, and examined the contribution of the gut microbiota. title: Ultra-Endurance Exercise Modifies Microbiota-Associated Amino Acid Metabolites Concurrent with Signs of Gut Barrier Injury.
abstract: Extreme endurance exercise disrupts gastrointestinal function, yet its effects on microbiota-associated metabolism remain poorly understood. Microbial metabolism of aromatic amino acids (ArAAs) generates bioactive indole- and phenol-derived compounds, including aryl-lactates and aryl-acetates, with distinct and potentially opposing effects on host physiology. title: Fermented Polygonatum kingianum polysaccharide exerts enhanced anti-obesity effects by modulating the gut microbiota-GDCA-TGR5 axis.
abstract: Probiotic-fermented Polygonatum kingianum polysaccharide (FPKP0) was previously confirmed to exhibit enhanced anti-adipogenic activity in 3T3-L1 cells in vitro owing to altered structural, prompting an examination of whether this modified FPKP0 exerts superior anti-obesity effects in vivo via related mechanism in high-fat diet-fed mice. journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

title: Camellia nitidissima Chi flower extract ameliorates alcoholic liver disease by reshaping bile acid homeostasis and intestinal barrier function.
abstract: Bile acid (BA) dyshomeostasis and intestinal barrier dysfunction are critical drivers of alcoholic liver disease (ALD), for which effective pharmacotherapies remain limited. Although Camellia nitidissima Chi flower possesses anti-inflammatory, hepatoprotective, and microbiota-modulatory properties, its role in ALD remains unclear.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

title: Colonic administration of baitouweng decoction alleviates ulcerative colitis via coordinated reprogramming of arginine and tryptophan metabolism.
abstract: Ulcerative colitis (UC) involves persistent colonic inflammation, loss of epithelial barrier integrity, and disturbed immune regulation. Although Baitouweng decoction (BTW) is widely used for intestinal inflammatory disorders, the effects and mechanisms of colon-targeted administration remain unclear.
journal: Phytomedicine : international journal of phytotherapy and phytopharmacology

title: Nutritional interventions in neonatal sepsis prevention & treatment.
abstract: Neonatal sepsis remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, particularly among preterm infants with profound immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal immaturity. Optimizing nutrition represents a promising yet complex strategy to support immune function, preserve gut integrity, and improve outcomes in this high-risk population. title: Fecal microbiota transplantation modulates immunosuppressive cells and IgA secretion in a gut microbiota depletion model.
abstract: The relationship between gut dysbiosis and host immune dynamics remains poorly understood. We used an antibiotic-induced gut microbiota depletion model following fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT) via co-housing. Mice received an antibiotic cocktail for 4 weeks (Abx group), or for 2 weeks, followed by co-housing with healthy control mice for 2 weeks (CoA group), or kept under conventional housing for 2 weeks (Abx-CH group). title: The Lactylation Landscape in Colorectal Cancer: from Metabolic-epigenetic Crosstalk to Precision Therapy.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) is fundamentally characterized by metabolic reprogramming, specifically the Warburg effect, which contributes to a lactate-enriched tumor microenvironment (TME) even under normoxic conditions. Transcending its traditional role as a metabolic byproduct, accumulated lactate functions as a substrate for lysine lactylation (Kla), a pervasive post-translational modification that bridges glycolytic flux with epigenetic remodeling. title: A Potential Probiotic Candidate Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 is Associated with Increased Intestinal Stem Cell-Mediated Proliferation and Altered Barrier-Related Parameters: Potential Involvement of the Wnt/β-Catenin Pathway.
abstract: Probiotic properties of the rumen-derived strain Heyndrickxia ginsengihumi W1 were evaluated by whole-genome analysis, in vitro assays, and a short-term mouse model. Genome analysis preliminarily indicated no acquired antimicrobial resistance genes or virulence factors. In mice, W1 administration showed no obvious adverse effects under the present short-term experimental conditions, and was associated with Lactobacillus enrichment and elevated lactate in the jejunum. title: Characterization of potential probiotic Lactobacillus spp. isolated from commercially reared pigs.
abstract: Probiotic bacteria and their products have shown significant promise as alternatives to traditional antimicrobials in the pig husbandry due to their antimicrobial activity. This study describes the comprehensive characterization of potential probiotic isolates sourced from the feces of commercial pig herds. title: Evaluation of Glutamate Manganese as an Alternative to Manganese Carbonate in Mice Diets: Tissue Manganese Deposition, Serum Antioxidant Status, Relative Bioavailability and Gut Multi-Omics Responses.
abstract: Manganese (Mn) is an essential trace element that supports redox balance, lipid metabolism, and liver function in animals. Mn deficiency can lead to decreased antioxidant capacity, poor development, and metabolic disorders. Glutamate Mn, as a new type of organic Mn source, has the characteristics of high absorption rate and good biological stability. title: [Research progress on the mechanism of acupuncture in protecting the intestinal barrier to intervene in Parkinson's disease].
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is the second most common neurodegenerative disorder worldwide. Accumulating evidence from recent years indicates a strong association between PD pathogenesis and gut-brain axis dysfunction, with impairment of the intestinal barrier being recognized as a critical initiating factor. title: Lactobacillus-derived threonine mediates the protective effect of piceatannol against endometritis.
abstract: Bacterial endometritis reflects a convergence of persistent infection, barrier failure, and excessive inflammation, yet how the gut microbiota influences these processes remains poorly understood. Here, we show that piceatannol (PIC) alleviates Escherichia coli-induced endometritis through a microbiota-dependent mechanism that limits uterine injury and preserves epithelial barrier function. title: Discovery of Human Gut Bacteria Responsible for Biotransformation and Structural Diversification of Oat Steroidal Saponins.
abstract: Oat steroidal saponins undergo biotransformation by the gut microbiota, yet the bacteria involved and the structural diversity of the resulting metabolites remain incompletely characterized. Incubation of avenacoside B (AVE-B), a major oat steroidal saponin, with fecal microbiota from six human donors revealed marked interindividual variation in avenacoside E (AVE-E) production. title: Oxygen-responsive bacterial glycosphingolipid links symbiont fitness and immune development in neonatal host.
abstract: Symbiotic gut bacteria must re-establish themselves in every host generation, yet the molecular strategies enabling this inheritance remain poorly understood. Here, we show that Bacteroides fragilis uses a membrane glycolipid, alpha-galactosylceramide (BfaGC), to colonize the neonatal gut. title: Heat-Inactivated Akkermansia muciniphila Reduces Viability Under Non-Adherent Conditions and Alters MUC13 and Survival-Related Gene Expression in Colorectal Cancer Cells.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) progression and metastasis are driven by molecular mechanisms that promote cell survival, migration, and resistance to anoikis. Current evidence indicates that the gut microbiota can actively influence these processes. Therefore, the main goal of this study was to investigate the impact of Akkermansia muciniphila on CRC aggressiveness by assessing gene expression, migration, and anoikis. title: Vagus nerve stimulation ameliorates epilepsy via a gut microbiota-butyrate-vagal axis.
abstract: Vagus nerve stimulation (VNS) is a therapy for drug-resistant epilepsy, yet its mechanisms are incompletely understood. We demonstrate that VNS modulates the gut microbiome and alters butyrate levels to reduce seizure susceptibility via vagus nerve-dependent signaling. In a longitudinal cohort of patients with epilepsy, VNS enriched short-chain fatty acid-producing bacteria, including Akkermansia muciniphila, Prevotella, Alistipes, and Odoribacter. title: Acetate-FFAR2 signaling induces neutrophil-derived IL-22 to protect against colitis.
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs) produced by gut microbiota are key modulators of intestinal homeostasis and immune responses. Although their anti-inflammatory roles are well established, the mechanisms by which SCFAs-FFAR2 shapes neutrophil function and influences intestinal inflammation remain unclear. title: Exploratory fecal metabolomics reveals potential metabolic signatures in girls with idiopathic central precocious puberty - a pilot study.
abstract: This study utilized an untargeted metabolomics approach to preliminarily investigate changes in fecal metabolites in girls with idiopathic central precocious puberty (ICPP) before and after treatment with gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) analogues.
journal: Journal of pediatric endocrinology & metabolism : JPEM

title: Lactate-induced PRDX1 lactylation increases the number of IgA plasma cells to confer exercise-mimicking protection against IBD.
abstract: Regular exercise enhances immune fitness and reduces disease risk; however, how it mobilizes immunity for disease prevention and key therapeutic targets remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a gut IgA-producing plasma cell subset (FSPhigh IgA PCs) that is functionally induced by exercise and characterized by high expression of the endoplasmic reticulum (ER)-related genes Fkbp11, Ssr2, and Ppib (collectively FSP). title: Dysbiosis in the gut microbiota and arginine and proline metabolism is associated with cognitive decline in aging.
abstract: Aging represents a severe health concern and causes various manifestations including neurodegeneration and metabolic dysfunction. The gut-brain axis has been implicated in cognitive aging. However, the associations of specific gut microbiota and metabolites with age-related cognitive decline remain poorly defined.

title: Neuroinflammation in Parkinson's disease: from glial heterogeneity and gut-brain immune crosstalk to precision therapeutic strategies.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss, α-synuclein pathology, and a broad spectrum of motor and non-motor manifestations. title: Cutaneous SCFAs are reduced in infantile atopic dermatitis and the SCFA-sensing receptor GPR43 modulates skin barrier integrity and inflammation.
abstract: Early-life skin colonization by commensal microbes is associated with a reduced risk of atopic dermatitis (AD), but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Regulatory effects of commensal gut bacteria are mediated in part by short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), metabolites generated during fiber fermentation. title: Fermented Sasa quelpaertensis-Supplemented Milk Attenuates UVB-Induced Skin Photoaging and Alters Gut Microbial and Short-Chain Fatty Acid Profiles.
abstract: Ultraviolet B (UVB) exposure accelerates skin photoaging by promoting extracellular matrix degradation, inflammatory responses, and epidermal barrier dysfunction. This study investigated the protective effects of Sasa quelpaertensis-supplemented milk (MSQ) and fermented S. quelpaertensis-supplemented milk (FMSQ), prepared using Lactobacillus gasseri KML25, in UVB-exposed HaCaT keratinocytes and SKH-1 hairless mice. title: Role of Bile Acids in Colorectal Diseases.
abstract: Bile acids (BAs) have functions well beyond fat digestion. They also serve as signals linking the gut microbiota to gut health. This review examines how BAs affect colorectal diseases and how this knowledge can guide diagnosis and treatment.

title: Perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 is associated with gut dysbiosis, impaired serotonin-kynurenine pathways and is linked to psychiatric-like disorders in rat offspring.
abstract: The prevalence of neurodegenerative diseases and psychiatric disorders, including anxiety and depression, appears to be higher among patients with gastrointestinal diseases, supporting the existence of a functional communication in the "gut-brain axis", that remains poorly described. title: Indole-3-lactic acid from gut microbiota suppresses colorectal cancer through AHR-ZBP1 signaling and PANoptosis-like cell death.
abstract: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains a major global health burden. This study observed reduced relative abundance of sequences assigned to Roseburia inulinivorans in patients with CRC. R. inulinivorans-derived cell-free supernatant (CFS) reduced CRC cell viability and clonogenic capacity and decreased tumor burden in an azoxymethane/dextran sulfate sodium model. title: Co-exposure to bisphenol A and ofloxacin induces oxidative stress and energy metabolic dysfunction while altering mobile genetic element composition and enriching specific antibiotic resistance genes in Meretrix petechialis.
abstract: Bisphenol A (BPA) and ofloxacin (OFL) are ubiquitous contaminants in aquatic environments and may pose combined risks to aquatic organisms. Although the toxic effects of BPA or OFL have been extensively investigated, the impacts of their co-exposure on intestinal health and antibiotic resistance in marine bivalves remain poorly understood. title: The inhibitory effect and mechanism of allicin combined with propolis extract on Cryptosporidiumparvum.
abstract: This study investigated the therapeutic potential of allicin combined with ethanolic propolis extract (ABP) and allicin combined with aqueous propolis extract (AWBP) against cryptosporidiosis. Results of molecular docking indicated that ABP could efficiently target the active pockets of lactate dehydrogenase (LDH) and ATP translocase in C. parvum, and stably bind to key amino acid residues through hydrogen bonds and hydrophobic interactions. title: Microbiota-gut-brain Axis in Autism Spectrum Disorder: Mechanistic Insights, Experimental and Clinical Evidence, and Therapeutic Perspectives.
abstract: Autism Spectrum Disorder (ASD) is a neurodevelopmental condition characterized by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity, arising from an interplay of genetic vulnerability, immune, metabolic, and gastrointestinal dysfunction, and neurobiological alterations. The bidirectional communication between the gut microbiota and the brain via neural, immune, endocrine, and microbial- metabolite pathways may contribute to ASD pathophysiology. title: Maternal gluten diet exacerbates offspring autistic-like behaviors through the gut-brain axis mediated by gut microbial metabolite elaidic acid.
abstract: Autism spectrum disorder (ASD) is a heterogeneous group of neurodevelopmental conditions characterized by social deficits and stereotyped behaviors, for which effective treatments remain lacking. Here we investigated whether early-life gluten exposure exacerbates autism-like behaviors in BTBR mice and explored the underlying microbiota-metabolite-brain mechanism. title: High-throughput screening of patient iPSC-derived neurons identifies the gut microbial metabolites that attenuate Alzheimer's disease pathology.
abstract: Gut microbiota-derived metabolites influence the gut-brain axis and may impact Alzheimer's disease (AD) pathology. However, the microbial metabolites involved in this process and their functional roles are largely unknown. We screened 352 gut metabolites in induced pluripotent stem cells (iPSC)-derived neurons from individuals with AD to identify compounds that reduce tau hyperphosphorylation. title: Formation of an inulin biocorona on food-grade titanium dioxide nanoparticles alleviates gut microbiota dysbiosis and inflammatory responses under calorie restriction.
abstract: Food-grade nanoparticles undergo dynamic interactions with dietary biomolecules during gastrointestinal transit, leading to the formation of a biomolecular corona that determines their biological identity and health effects. Here, we investigated whether an inulin-derived biocorona could modulate the gastrointestinal fate and biological responses of the nanoscale fraction of titanium dioxide (TiO2) under normal and calorie-restricted conditions. title: A NanAKE-like pathway enables sialic acid catabolism in gut microbiome member Hungatella hathewayi.
abstract: Sialic acids are abundant components of host- and diet-derived glycans in the human gut that shape microbial fitness and interspecies competition. Free sialic acids can be a nutrient source but also stimulate inflammation and pathogen colonization. Escherichia coli and Bacteroides spp. catabolize sialic acids via the NanAKE and NanLE-RokA pathways, yet the metabolic capacity of many microbiome members remains undefined. title: Akkermansia muciniphila extracellular vesicles enhance immunotherapy and suppress liver cancer by delivering a ferroptosis-inducing protein.
abstract: Modulation of the gut microbiome is a promising therapeutic strategy for enhancing cancer immunotherapy. Here, we report that Akkermansia muciniphila (A. muciniphila), a mucin-degrading bacterium, exhibits protective effects against liver cancer (LC) progression and improves immunotherapy efficacy. We find that LC patients unresponsive to immunotherapy show depleted A. muciniphila abundance. Oral gavage of A. muciniphila attenuates LC in mice. title: Parasitic infections as upstream drivers of the gut-kidney axis: Dysbiosis, uremic toxin generation, and renal injury - A comprehensive narrative review.
abstract: The intestinal dysbiosis-renal axis works in both directions: Chronic kidney disease (CKD) and acute kidney injury (AKI) lead to gut dysbiosis, loss of short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), and buildup of uremic toxins. This comprehensive narrative review (assessed using SANRA) inspects parasitic infections as upstream factors that disrupt the intestinal barrier and microbiota, thereby causing renal injury. title: Diet correction after perinatal deficiency in vitamin B9 and B12 fails to rescue gut dysbiosis, serotonin pathway and psychiatric-like behavior in adult rats.
abstract: Perinatal dietary deficiencies such as vitamin B9 and B12 induce persistent gut dysbiosis, metabolic, physiologic imbalances and behavioral defects that could extend into adulthood, but the underlying fetal programming mechanisms remain poorly understood. We have investigated the long-term consequences of a perinatal vitamin B9 and B12 deficiency associated dysbiosis and focusing on sex-dependent outcomes related to behavior and molecular markers of the gut-brain axis. title: Gut microbial PncA as a potential target to elevate NAD⁺ biosynthetic flux for delaying aging.
abstract: Dysregulation of nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NAD⁺) metabolic homeostasis is a key driver of aging. Because NAD⁺ biosynthetic flux directly reflects the actual rate of NAD⁺ production in cells and tissues, enhancing NAD⁺ biosynthetic flux plays a positive role in restoring its metabolic homeostasis and delaying aging. title: Primary sclerosing cholangitis: epidemiology, risk factors, pathophysiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and management.
abstract: Primary sclerosing cholangitis (PSC) is a rare cholangiopathy characterized by multifocal inflammation and fibrostenotic remodeling of the bile ducts, cholestasis, and increased risks of cholangiocarcinoma and colorectal cancer. No pharmacological therapy has yet improved transplant-free survival. Clinical care therefore depends on accurate phenotyping, surveillance, treatment of biliary and intestinal complications, and timely liver transplantation. title: BGN4-derived intestinal metabolite 6-hydroxynicotinic acid alleviates hepatocytes ferroptosis in MAFLD via Nrf2/SREBP1/CYP2E1 axis.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) is closely associated with dysbiosis of the gut microbiota. In this study, we investigated the biological effects and underlying mechanisms of Bifidobacterium bifidum BGN4 and its intestinal metabolite, 6-hydroxynicotinic acid (6-HNA), in regulating hepatocyte ferroptosis in MAFLD.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences

title: Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 attenuates high-salt-induced hypertension involving IL-17A signaling suppression.
abstract: Chronic high-salt (HS) intake induces hypertension and is associated with reduced intestinal Lactobacillus. This study investigated underlying mechanisms for Lactobacillus plantarum CCFM639 (CCFM639) alleviating HS-induced hypertension.

title: Comparative Genomic Diversity, Gut Microbiota Modulation, and 28-Day Oral Tolerability of Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATA-LTC-Lr050600.
abstract: The rational development of microbiota-targeted therapeutics requires a combined assessment of the physiological effects of candidate microorganisms on the host and their ecological effects on the gut microbiota. The present study evaluates the toxicological properties and gut microbiota-related effects of a newly identified microorganism, designated as the Limosilactobacillus reuteri ATA-LTC-Lr050600 strain. title: The Gut Microbiota: A Critical Mediator in Particulate Matter-Induced Health Risks.
abstract: Environmental particulate matter (PM), particularly fine particles (PM2.5), coarse particles (PM10), and ultrafine particles (UFPs), pose a major public health threat. Emerging evidence identifies the gut microbiota as a key mediator through which PM exposure induces systemic health effects. Exposure to PM disrupts microbial diversity and structure throughout the life cycle. This disruption is characterized by a loss of beneficial microbes and an increase in potentially harmful ones. title: Gut microbiota-driven imbalance of the gut-brain-immune homeostatic network in constipation: Pathogenic mechanisms and evolving therapeutic prospects.
abstract: Chronic constipation (CC) is increasingly recognized as a systems-level disorder that cannot be explained by impaired intestinal motility alone. Here, we integrate evidence from clinical cohorts, animal models, and mechanistic studies to examine how gut microbial dysbiosis and altered microbial metabolites perturb epithelial barrier integrity, immune homeostasis, enteric neural activity, and gut-brain signaling. title: Tryptophan metabolism in autoimmune diseases: From homeostatic regulator to pathological amplifier.
abstract: Tryptophan metabolism serves as a critical hub linking nutrient sensing, gut microbiota, and immune regulation, playing an essential role in maintaining immune homeostasis. Accumulating evidence indicates that dysregulated tryptophan metabolism is a shared pathological feature of multiple immune-mediated diseases, including systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), rheumatoid arthritis (RA), multiple sclerosis (MS), and inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). Adult female zebrafish were exposed to 5,000 ng/L CIP for 30 days and evaluated using histology, hormone assays, metagenomics, metabolomics, transcriptomics, and fecal microbiota transplantation (FMT). title: Antiruisi Attenuates Atherosclerosis in High-Fat-Diet-Fed ApoE-/- Mice and Is Associated with Alterations in the Gut Microbiota.
abstract: Atherosclerosis is a leading cause of cardiovascular morbidity and mortality, and the gut microbiota is a potential therapeutic target. Antiruisi (ATRS) is a fixed-ratio combination of natural-product-derived active ingredients. In this study, 24 male ApoE-/- mice were assigned to normal chow, high-fat diet (HFD), HFD plus atorvastatin, or HFD plus ATRS groups (n = 6 per group) and treated for 12 weeks. title: Salinity-Driven Nonadditive Disruption of Digestive Energy Homeostasis in Mussels by Titanium Dioxide Nanoparticles.
abstract: Titanium dioxide nanoparticles (TiO2 NPs) are increasingly accumulating in coastal waters. Seasonal salinity fluctuations further complicate their ecological risks. We investigated how salinity modulates TiO2 NP toxicity on digestive energy metabolism in the thick-shelled mussel Mytilus coruscus, an important coastal economic shellfish. abstract: Codonopsis lanceolata root peel, which is commonly discarded as an agro-industrial byproduct, was investigated as a potential source of gut health-promoting components. The present study evaluated the intestinal protective effects and growth-supporting potential of an aqueous C. lanceolata root peel extract (CPE). title: Isolation, identification and prebiotic potential of polysaccharides from fresh goji berry.
abstract: Polysaccharides from fresh goji berry were isolated and characterized to investigate their structures, simulated gastrointestinal digestion, and lactic acid bacteria (LAB) growth-supporting effects. Hot-water extraction, 50% ethanol precipitation, and chromatographic separation yielded two acidic polysaccharides, LBP1 and LBP2, with apparent molecular weights of 13.47 ± 0.24 and 185.0 ± 3.0 kDa, respectively. title: Development of Type 2 Diabetes During Aging Shifts the Brain Metabolome and Gut Microbiome in a Sex-Dependent Manner.
abstract: Background/Objectives: The development of type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) is a major risk factor for cognitive decline and dementia. Both T2DM and aging are associated with alterations in brain metabolism and gut microbiome composition. However, the effects of age-related metabolic dysfunction during the development of T2DM on the brain metabolome and gut-brain axis (GBA), particularly with respect to sex-specific differences, remain poorly understood. title: High-throughput screening identifies Limosilactobacillus reuteri HBNK04 as a potent antiviral probiotic against porcine epidemic diarrhea virus.
abstract: Porcine epidemic diarrhea virus (PEDV) continues to cause substantial economic losses to the swine industry, and current vaccines and biosecurity measures remain insufficient to prevent viral spread. Probiotics have emerged as promising microecological interventions due to their capacity to inhibit pathogens and modulate host immunity. title: Oral live and heat-killed Ligilactobacillus salivarius Ls.0403 alleviate MC903-induced atopic dermatitis-like inflammation and are associated with gut microbiota changes in mice.
abstract: Atopic dermatitis (AD) is a chronic, relapsing inflammatory skin disease that often requires long-term management. Probiotics have been investigated as adjunctive approaches for AD, but their effects are highly strain specific. Among these, Ligilactobacillus salivarius has shown potential in previous AD studies, yet the effects of different strains remain insufficiently characterized. title: Microbiome-dependent phytosterol sulfates production and tissue distribution in mice.
abstract: Microbial biotransformation of dietary lipids, such as cholesterol, influences host homeostasis. Despite extensive studies on animal sterols in host-microbiota interactions, the role of phytosterols in homeostasis remains unclear. In this study, we characterized phytosterol sulfates as microbiota-derived metabolites using untargeted lipidomic data mining. title: Functional feed additive intervention strategies for necrotic enteritis in broiler chickens: a perspective on host-pathogen interactions and the gut microbiota.
abstract: Necrotic enteritis (NE) threatens intestinal health and productivity in broiler chickens, prompting growing interest in nutritional interventions amid restrictions on in-feed antibiotic use. NE pathogenesis involves Clostridium perfringens (C. perfringens) virulence, mucosal injury, and alterations in the gut microbiota and its metabolic environment, processes that may interact to influence disease progression. title: Multiomic crosstalk between plasma metabolites and inflammation in IBD via MR and mouse validation.
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) is a chronic relapsing inflammatory disorder characterized by gut dysbiosis and recurrent intestinal inflammation. Integrating bibliometric analysis, two-sample Mendelian randomization (MR), cross-platform protein pQTL MR, colocalization, and druggability assessment, we dissected gut microbiota-driven plasma metabolite-inflammation homeostasis axes in IBD. title: Gut microbiota composition of India's Baiga tribe: Insights from an indigenous particularly vulnerable tribal group.
abstract: The transition from traditional foraging lifestyles to modernized urban environments is associated with reduced human gut microbiome diversity. To examine this shift within the Indian subcontinent, we used shotgun metagenomics to compare the gut microbiota of 50 adults: 25 from the indigenous, foraging, and particularly vulnerable Baiga tribe and 25 from an urban population in Bhopal, Central India. title: D-Xylose Attenuates High-Fat Diet-Induced Obesity Potentially via Modulation of Gut Microbiota and Cecal Lipidome in Mice.
abstract: Obesity and its associated metabolic complications pose a significant global public health challenge. This study systematically investigated the effects of D-xylose on gut microbiota structure and cecal lipid metabolism in a high-fat diet (HFD)-induced obese mouse model. title: A putative model of the gut-muscle axis in aged livestock
abstract: The gut-muscle axis has been proposed to link gut microbiota with skeletal muscle physiology, yet its universality across livestock species remains unclear. title: Akkermansia muciniphila alleviates cytarabine-induced myelosuppression by remodeling gut microbiota and restoring butyrate-mediated hematopoietic recovery.
abstract: Currently, chemotherapy remains the mainstream treatment for acute myeloid leukemia, yet it frequently causes severe toxicities, with myelosuppression being the most common and clinically consequential.

title: Metabolic interplay of SCFA’s in the gut and oral microbiome: a link to health and disease
abstract: Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), primarily acetate (C2), propionate (C3), and butyrate (C4), are crucial microbial metabolites formed by the fermentation of dietary fibers by gut microbiota in the colon. These SCFAs, characterized by fewer than six carbon atoms, serve as an essential energy source for colonic epithelial cells and contribute approximately 10% of the body's total energy requirement. title: Impact of microplastics on the human gut microbiome: a systematic review of microbial composition, diversity, and metabolic disruptions
abstract: Global plastic waste production remains a critical environmental issue. Microplastics (MPs), plastic particles less than 5 mm, are now pervasive across ecosystems. Humans are exposed to MPs via ingestion, inhalation, and dermal contact raising concerns about their health impacts. title: Gut microbiome-mediated health effects of fiber and polyphenol-rich dietary interventions
abstract: Dietary components substantially influence aging-related health outcomes through the interaction with the gut microbiome. In this narrative review, we compiled human dietary intervention trials with varying complexities: from simple modifications like the addition of herbs and spices, nuts and beans, to whole-diet patterns such as the calorie-restricted high-polyphenol Green-Mediterranean diet. title: Short-chain fatty acids—a key link between the gut microbiome and T-lymphocytes in neonates?
abstract: Infancy is a vulnerable and critical phase in the acquisition of the gut microbiome and the establishment of immune function. Short-chain fatty acids (SCFAs), such as acetate, propionate and butyrate, are compounds mostly produced by the microbiome through various metabolic pathways and play an indispensable role in connecting the microbiome and the adaptive immune system. title: Gut microbiome remodeling in chronic kidney disease: implications of kidney replacement therapies and therapeutic interventions
abstract: The escalating global burden of end-stage renal disease (ESRD), driven by aging populations and rising metabolic comorbidities, underscores the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. Emerging evidence highlights the gut microbiome as a pivotal modulator of renal pathophysiology through the gut-kidney axis, with microbial dysbiosis exacerbating gut microbial metabolites (e.g., uremic toxins), systemic inflammation, and multi-organ damage. title: Microbiome-derived bile acids contribute to elevated antigenic response and bone erosion in rheumatoid arthritis
abstract: Rheumatoid arthritis (RA) is a chronic, disabling and incurable autoimmune disease. It has been widely recognized that gut microbial dysbiosis is an important contributor to the pathogenesis of RA, although distinct alterations in microbiota have been associated with this disease. title: The blue dragon nudibranch (Glaucus atlanticus) shifts to less venomous prey in the Mediterranean, with no evidence of defensive microbial symbionts
abstract: Glaucus atlanticus ("blue dragon"), is an aeolid nudibranch that acquires chemical defense through sequestration of nematocysts from its primary prey, the highly venomous Physalia physalis ("Portuguese man-of-war"). In August 2025 hundreds of G. atlanticus individuals appeared near Alicante (Spain), prompting temporary beach closures due to concerns about potential envenomation. abstract: Adherent-invasive Escherichia coli (AIEC) is a subtype of pathogenic E. coli associated with Crohn's disease. AIEC strains are characterized by the ability to adhere to and invade epithelial cells, survive and replicate within macrophages. Despite many years of research, the mechanisms of virulence and pathogenicity still remain not fully understood. abstract: Many Gram-negative bacterial pathogens rely on the type III secretion system (T3SS) to deliver virulence factors or effectors into host cells. In Vibrio parahaemolyticus, the leading cause of seafood-borne gastroenteritis, one of the two T3SSs, the T3SS2, is essential for intestinal colonization and infection in the human body. title: A microbiota-dependent fitness locus promotes intraspecies competition and cell envelope resilience in gut bacterium Phocaeicola vulgatus
abstract: A central question in gut microbial ecology is how dominant bacterial species establish and occupy their niches amid inter- and intraspecies competition.
